minutes.headline: Sewer Commission heard a consultant's preliminary I&I findings, abated a betterment, and clashed over a member's resignation.
minutes.summary: A consultant team presented a preliminary inflow and infiltration evaluation showing large gaps and inconsistencies in pump station data, with a final report about two months late. The commission voted to authorize the chair to sign a notarized document, abate a remaining betterment balance, and approve the Q4 commitment and prior minutes. The Town Meeting articles, year-to-date budget, RFP status and upcoming elections were discussed, and the chair and a member disputed whether the member had promised to resign.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to authorize the chair to sign a notarized document for 117 Mass Ave and to abate that property's remaining betterment balance.
A consultant team presented a preliminary inflow and infiltration evaluation that found gaps and inconsistencies in pump station data; the final report is about two months late.
The commission passed over the fourth Town Meeting article, the emergency article on the sewer budget, because the budget shows a buffer.
The Q4 sewer billing commitment was approved.
Members were asked to review the revised sewer operator RFP from town counsel and send comments, with the aim of getting it out to bid quickly.

why_it_matters: Sewer bills and the sewer budget are paid by users through rates, so the Q4 commitment and the question of whether the budget has a buffer bear directly on what residents are billed.
Unreliable pump station data and a late I&I report slow the work of finding where groundwater and stormwater enter the sewer system, and that work drives long-term sewer costs.
The operator RFP will decide who runs the system under a new contract, and the commission's budget review noted that the interim contractor's billing is far lower than the prior contractor's.
watch_next: Next meeting on the 30th, a brief session to organize officers after the election.
Irrigation fee non-payment enforcement is to be put on the next agenda, and the final I&I report is still due.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the main votes (betterment document, abatement, Q4 commitment of $206,382.29) and on passing over the 4th article. They differ on the property address (117 vs 1170 Mass Ave), the payment deadline (June 30 vs 6/29), several figures that appear only in ours, commissioner names, and the RFP and agenda decisions. The thing to check first is the vote tallies and commissioner names, since the official gives 5-0 and 4-0-1 counts and different surnames from ours.
